title: ChatGPT Mac Product-First Context Pack
summary: A stable-core plus rotating-snapshot context pack for ChatGPT Mac sessions that keeps Rig Relay focused on a polished product for developers and effective agents, without turning the pack into a governance encyclopedia.

sections.content: This pack is the low-maintenance default for ChatGPT Mac sessions. It keeps the north star on shipping a polished Rig Relay product that is delightful for developers and effective for agents, while keeping governance present but compressed.

items: What is the product trying to delight users with right now?
What boundaries keep agents effective without turning the system into a compliance project?
What current state matters now, and which pieces are safe to keep stable?

rows: Repo discipline, claim calibration, lane closure, git policy
Surface map and product surface hierarchy
Delight-oriented desktop UX and cockpit behavior
Desktop projection contract and surface expectations
What stays local, what may go remote, and why
Agent role boundaries and push/review gates
Tracks the current frontend/bridge/backend readiness snapshot
Refresh when the bridge contract, test surface, or readiness state changes
Captures the current cockpit/UI state and the product-facing experience
Refresh when the UI or user-facing surface changes
Captures the current GitHub/provider review operating picture
Refresh when GitHub-connected review, auth, or repository-access assumptions change

items: Keep the stable core fixed unless a doctrine change truly affects product shape or agent boundaries.
Refresh only the rotating trio when the current state changes; do not rewrite the whole pack just to reflect one new snapshot.
Do not add broad security, privacy, or cryptography doctrine unless the current task truly depends on it.
If the conversation drifts toward policy accumulation, pull it back to product delight, agent effectiveness, and the minimum safe boundary.

sections.content: How To Use It In ChatGPT Mac

items: Upload the stable core once and keep it fixed.
Upload or replace only the three rotating snapshot files when the current state changes.
Ask the model to answer product goal first, then user-facing surface, then agent/review boundary, then governance only if needed.
If a new task needs a different snapshot, swap one rotating file instead of changing the stable core.
